name: Holy Mission
english_description: A large (~24,000 .lpc file), heavily player-authored MudOS-lineage archive originally run out of Linz, Austria (the login banner reads 'Welcome to the Holy Mission at Linz, Austria'). Confirmed MudOS/FluffOS-compatible via a full-tree grep for driver_hook/set_driver_hook/H_[A-Z_]+ (zero hits) before porting. The mudlib is built almost entirely around two textually-#include'd (not inherit'd) base classes misfiled under doc/lib/ -- doc/lib/living.lpc and doc/lib/player.lpc -- both genuinely 3500+ line implementations despite living in a 'documentation' directory, while the canonical sys/living.lpc and sys/player.lpc files the rest of the archive expects were preserved as empty 0-byte placeholders (recovered by inheriting the real doc/lib/ classes from them). doc/lib/player.lpc does NOT inherit doc/lib/living.lpc (only secure/valid), so dozens of stat/state fields and helper functions (set_number_of_arms, query_gender/query_pronoun, query_real_name, follow/language systems, etc.) had to be independently re-added, ported verbatim from living.lpc's own copies. Several other genuinely-empty files (sys/include/sys_*.h, sys/savings.lpc, sys/living_defs.h) were reconstructed from cross-referenced wizard personal copies and doc/magik design docs. Key driver-compatibility fixes: this driver's file_name() always returns a leading '/' (broke numerous hardcoded path-prefix comparisons, most critically doc/lib/player.lpc's own logon() security check, which destructed every single login attempt with 'illegal logon: /secure/login#0' until fixed); creator_file() must always return a non-empty string (uid machinery requires it on every object load) which in turn required re-auditing every truthy creator()-check in the mudlib; classic alist/closure/lambda/2-arg move_object/2-arg command and about a dozen other missing classic efuns (getpwent/setpwent/addpwent, m_indices/m_values, cat, strstr, extract, isalpha, filter_objects, set_prompt, enable_interactive, set_modify_command, etc.) were reimplemented as simul_efun shims, several from scratch (a from-scratch pw_db-backed password database backing getpwent/setpwent, since the archive's own 1994-era comment says it moved off flat-file /secure/passwd/ onto an ndbm database this driver has no equivalent for). The most severe and novel finding this session (see AGENTS.md §7.177): a direct, explicit call to a function literally named 'reset' can silently no-op on this driver even when called eagerly from that very object's own create() -- confirmed independently in doc/lib/player.lpc (env_var/msgin/etc. never got initialized, crashing every 'score') and secure/simul_efun.lpc (the password database's own reset() never restored pw_db from disk, silently discarding every registered password across a driver restart) -- fixed by renaming the real logic to do_reset() and calling that directly, keeping reset() as a thin pass-through for the driver's own natural scheduled reset apply. A second, related finding (AGENTS.md §7.178): secure/master.lpc's wizard-level database was seeded only from a dead LDMud-only apply (inaugurate_master()) that this driver never calls at all, intermittently crashing get_wiz_level() on an ordinary player name depending on incidental compile-order timing; fixed with a real create(). A third significant, corpus-wide-shaped bug: this driver's own 'time to reset' is 1800 seconds, so a room compiled for the first time (e.g. a brand new character's actual starting room) sat completely dark and undescribed for up to half an hour; fixed at the universal ROOM base class (room/room.lpc) with a create() routed through call_other(this_object(),"reset",0) (a bare reset(0) call is unreliable per §7.177) -- reaches every room in the mudlib that doesn't define its own create(). A genuinely-lost-content file (obj/rsoul.lpc, a single #include of a wizard's own personal file that is completely absent from the archive under any name) was stubbed as an inert placeholder rather than reconstructed, since every new character unconditionally clones and moves it during setup. End-to-end verified live: register a brand-new character, confirm password, enter the game, pick a gender, see a fully lit and described starting room (race/room), list and choose a race (stats update correctly), move to the starting church with a full room description and exits, save, quit (which hands the connection back to a fresh login menu, itself real archived design, not a bug), and reconnect with the correct password across a full driver restart -- character state (race, stats, guild) persisted correctly. A wrong password is correctly rejected post-fix, confirming the password check is genuinely functional, not just bypassed.
